author: Perpetua of Carthage
work: The Passion of Perpetua and Felicitas
translation: R. E. Wallis (ANF vol. 3), public domain
note: From the prison diary of Perpetua, a young mother martyred at Carthage c. AD 203 — one of the earliest surviving texts written by a Christian woman. To her father begging her to recant, she answers with the pitcher that cannot be called anything but what it is. New voice for the corpus. Section follows the cited ANF/Wallis numbering (ch. 1); this is ch. 3 in the standard modern (Musurillo) numbering. New Advent files the whole Passio under Tertullian (an old, unproven conjecture that he edited the framing narrative), but this passage is from the first-person diary, which is genuinely Perpetua's. Verified verbatim against source_url (apologia-citations, web, 2026-08-24).
text: ‘Father,’ said I, ‘do you see, let us say, this vessel lying here to be a little pitcher, or something else?’ And he said, ‘I see it to be so.’ And I replied to him, ‘Can it be called by any other name than what it is?’ And he said, ‘No.’ ‘Neither can I call myself anything else than what I am, a Christian.’
